news.title: Ruby Rippey breaks cover after salacious essay exposed Gavin Newsom affair details
news.text:
Ruby Rippey, the former lover of Gov. Gavin Newsom who reignited one of California’s biggest political scandals with a bombshell Vanity Fair essay Tuesday, was spotted walking her dog just hours after the story went viral.

Dressed casually, Rippey appeared carefree and relaxed as she enjoyed a sunny afternoon near her Marin County home following publication of the essay, which thrust her decades-old affair with Newsom back into the national spotlight.

Rippey served as an aide to Newsom when he was mayor of San Francisco and was married at the time to his campaign manager and close friend, Alex Tourk.

In the essay, Rippey accuses Newsom of sanitizing one of the defining scandals of his political career, arguing the governor reshaped key details of their affair in his memoir, “Young Man in a Hurry,” which was released as the governor is widely expected to mount a 2028 presidential campaign.

Newsom described the relationship as “the stupidest and also briefest of affairs,” writing that Rippey “was among a group of staffers who came to my apartment for a party. She was the last to leave.”

But Rippey said reading the memoir left her with “a familiar feeling … of being written about by someone who assumes I won’t answer.”

“He describes it as ‘the briefest of affairs.’ His sister, he notes, observed that I was ‘hanging a bit too close,'” Rippey wrote.

Instead, the affair appears to have lasted for some time and sexual encounters occurred in multiple places and overnight stays.

She also disputed Newsom’s account of how her husband learned about the affair, challenging his suggestion that he was the one who came clean to Tourk.

“That detail — subtle but significant — is the one that stays with me,” Rippey wrote. “It reads — to me, at least — as a version of events that gives him credit for something I had already done. Technically defensible, perhaps, but one that leaves the unmistakable impression that he, not I, was the one who told Alex the truth.”

Newsom’s office declined comment on the essay.

The affair remains one of the biggest stains of Newsom’s life and political career. Tourk resigned after confronting the mayor, who later held a news conference calling the affair a “personal lapse of judgment.”

“I want to make it clear that everything you’ve heard and read is true, and I am deeply sorry about that,” Newsom said at the time.

Rippey’s essay also renewed scrutiny of comments made by Jennifer Siebel Newsom, who was dating the future governor when the affair became public and publicly placed much of the blame on Rippey.

“I shouldn’t say this, but … if people did research into the scandal … the woman is the culprit,” Siebel Newsom told the San Francisco Chronicle.

Siebel Newsom later doubled down in comments on the SFist blog despite describing herself as “a total woman’s woman.”

“I’m a total woman’s woman, girls girl … what’s your definition of affair? … It was a few nothing incidents when she showed up passed out outside of his door … she is bad news,” Siebel Newsom wrote.

She also defended Newsom, saying he was dealing with “crises — divorce, the loss of his mother, the pressures of being mayor, etc. and he was vulnerable and lonely.”

Siebel Newsom later apologized after the comments sparked backlash.

Download The California Post App, follow us on social, and subscribe to our newsletters 

Sam Singer, a spokesman for Rippey at the time, bashed Siebel Newsom for her comments.

“Ms. Siebel is an actress. I understand her need for publicity. However, her comments are unbecoming of an actress or a lady,” Singer said.

Rippey, who has since remarried and says she has remained sober for years, wrote that the affair began in 2005 while Newsom was separated from his then-wife, Kimberly Guilfoyle, and Rippey was married to Tourk. 

She acknowledged she willingly entered the relationship but said she now recognizes the power imbalance between a mayor and one of his subordinates.

“Still, the [#MeToo] reckoning exposed what I had missed: Power does not need to coerce. It only needs to exist,” Rippey wrote. “The responsibility to hold the line belongs to the one who holds it. That didn’t happen. But I didn’t stumble into the space left open — I saw a possibility and went for it.”

She added, “Both things are true: I am responsible for what I did. Power does not distribute consequences evenly.”

Rippey also revealed that Kamala Harris, who at that time was San Francisco’s district attorney and still years away from becoming vice president, privately reached out after the scandal broke and urged her to stay silent.

“‘Just pause,” Harris told Rippey, according to the essay. “More time will give you better perspective.'”
news.summary: Ruby Rippey, the former lover of Gov. Gavin Newsom who reignited one of California's biggest political scandals with a bombshell Vanity Fair essay Tuesday, was spotted walking her dog just hours after the story went viral.
news.author: Annie Gaus

news.title: Why Mark Ruffalo is missing from Spider-Man: Brand New Day's press tour: Spoiler fears, Palestine support, or a busy schedule?
news.text: While Tom Holland and Zendaya are doing the media rounds like the pros they are, one massive name has been conspicuously absent from the Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour. Mark Ruffalo, who is set to appear as Bruce Banner/The Hulk in the upcoming blockbuster, is nowhere to be found. No talk show appearances, red carpets, or carefully worded interviews where he almost spills the beans. It's almost as if Marvel has placed a permanent mute button on the man. But given his track record, can you really blame them?When it comes to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Mark Ruffalo is basically the cast member who you hand a sock to and tell him to sit in the corner. In 2017, the 58-year-old casually dropped that in the next movie, "everybody dies" on Good Morning America.This was, of course, a major spoiler for Avengers: Infinity War. Poor Don Cheadle was sitting right next to him, looking like he wanted to phase through the floor. And it wasn't a one-off mistake. Ruffalo previously accidentally live-streamed the audio of the Thor: Ragnarok premiere on Instagram for 10 minutes before realising. He would basically have been a PR nightmare wrapped in green spandex for director Destin Daniel Cretton.Pairing Mark Ruffalo and Tom Holland for promotional interviews is like leaving two toddlers unattended in a room full of explosives. Marvel learned their lesson the hard way. Benedict Cumberbatch, who had the unenviable task of sharing the press tour with Holland, once described feeling like his "babysitter," claiming it was like "avoiding grenades coming from the right and left". Can you imagine what would happen if Marvel unleashed both Ruffalo and Holland on the same interviewer? It would be chaos.While his spoiler habit is legendary, Ruffalo's absence is also being connected to his outspoken politics. A staunch critic of Donald Trump and his policies, he has been a vocal supporter of Palestine, recently backing the historical film Palestine 36 through a series of special screenings and conversations.The film, which explores the Arab revolt against British colonial rule in 1936, is described as "one of the greatest and most important films" about the history of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Ruffalo's known for his leftist views, even helping organise an Avengers-themed video to support Kamala Harris. In the current political climate, Disney might have thought it wise to keep their star away from any potential on-camera eruptions. Believers of this theory believe this could have been Rachel Zegler's Snow White promotion had Ruffalo been involved.There is a more boring but practical explanation for Ruffalo's absence from the Spider-Man press tour. According to reports, Ruffalo is currently busy shooting the second season of the HBO crime drama Task. The show began production in Philadelphia earlier this month, making it logistically difficult for him to join the promotional circuit. However, Marvel has a history of hiding their actors from the press due to their track record, so the "busy schedule" excuse might just be a convenient cover for "we can't trust him anywhere near a microphone."Fans have taken to social media with their theories, and they're not holding back. One user on X hilariously pointed out, "Marvel learned their lesson after Infinity War.... Mark Ruffalo giving promotional interviews for Spider-Man: Brand New Day would just mean the entire plot gets spoiled in 5 minutes flat. Marvel keeping him away from mics is top-tier strategy." Another simply said, "Probably cos Marvel would snipe him for accidentally spoiling smth again."Some have highlighted his political views as the real reason. One commenter said, "Because he runs his mouth about the president too much and marvel seems like they want a home run hit." Another harshly added, "Excellent, we don't want to hear is crazy leftist views when thinking about the Hulk."Whether it's due to his history of spoiling movies, his political firebrand status, or just a simple scheduling conflict, keeping Mark Ruffalo away from the Spider-Man microphones might just be the smartest PR decision Marvel has made in years. The guy is a fantastic actor, but when it comes to keeping secrets, he makes the Hulk look like a master of subtlety.Spider-Man: Brand New Day releases in theatres on July 31. In India, the movie has an early release, coming to theatres on July 30.

news.title: Kamala Harris 'Told Gavin Newsom's Former Mistress to Pause and Not Make a Public Comment' About Their Steamy Affair
news.text:
Former Vice President Kamala Harris has been dragged into California Governor Gavin Newsom's latest scandal.

The woman who had an affair with Newsom, Ruby Rippey, claimed Harris encouraged her to stay silent about the affair back in 2005. With that feedback in mind, Rippey, who was an aide under Newsom at the time, remained quiet until now, RadarOnline.com has learned.Kamala Harris Offers Ruby Rippey AdviceAt the time, Newsom was the mayor of San Francisco. When the press heard news of an affair in his office, Newsom's girlfriend at the time publicly played down the fling, chalking it up to "a few nothing incidents." 

Rippey was publicly branded "bad news."

She was offered opportunities to speak, according to her explosive essay in Vanity Fair, including a potential memoir offer. However, Harris, who was the district attorney at the time, gave her a phone call.

Rippey recalled Harris, whom she called "a real girl's girl," allegedly telling her, "I wouldn’t say anything right now, Ruby. Just pause. More time will give you better perspective."

Harris' guidance was "the best advice I received," confessed Rippey. She reflected, realizing at the time she was still fresh into the emotional turbulence, "unable to make sense of anything, let alone speak clearly about it." 

Rippey resolved, "So I stayed silent."Rippey Opens Up About California ScandalThe affair, which first went public in 2007, lasted intermittently from 2005 to 2006. Rippey was married at the time to Newsom's campaign manager Alex Tourk. Newsom, while separated from then-wife Kimberly Guilfoyle, was still legally married, with the divorce not yet finalized.

While the relationship didn't officially begin until 2005, Rippey claimed she felt the weight of Newsom's desire starting in 2004. She claimed in her essay he noticed him "looking at me." 

Plus, she recalled the 58-year-old telling her, "You look really good." Rippey leaned into the desire, becoming more intentional with the clothes she wore to the office.Gavin Newsom and Rippey's Affair Begins in 2005In July 2005, Rippey recalled attending a wedding in Napa Valley. When the night turned to partying, her husband chose to leave while Rippey went back to an inn with Newsom.

She wrote, "I wake the next morning beside him, still dressed. I am cold, almost shivering, and my dress – the one my mother warned me not to wear – is soaked from the waist down. I had passed out."

"The boundaries begin to disintegrate," she claimed. It wasn't necessarily discreet, as Rippey claimed others in the office began to notice.

Nonetheless, they continued to meet periodically. She penned, "We meet, and we drink. There is s--, but it isn’t the point. The point is proximity – to power, to being chosen, to feeling newly visible."

For Rippey, "it feels like oxygen."Rippey Accuses Newsom of Inaccuracies in MemoirUltimately, Rippey resigned from her post in 2006 after battling with drugs and alcohol. She decided to get sober, which she did not believe would be possible in her professional position nor while staying in the affair. 

She maintained the affair was not what caused her downward spiral, but rather it "just gave it somewhere to live."

In 2007, Rippey penned an email to her husband with the confession before returning home from rehab. When she returned home, Tourk was "measured" in his response. When Tourk eventually confronted Newsom, Rippey claimed, "there is no straight answer" about the affair. 

Tourk's resignation sparked the media hysteria which would ultimately lead to Rippey's call with Harris. Newsom owned up to the affair. 

"Everything you've heard and read is true," he claimed. 

Rippey was later inspired to come forward after Newsom penned his own memoir. 

In the pages of the text, according to Rippey, Newsom downplayed their relationship. 

Plus, she alleged, Newsom falsely claimed he was the one who eventually confessed to Tourk.

news.title: Trump’s ‘embarrassing’ comment about LeBron has ESPN host speaking up: ‘Beyond the pale"
news.text:
It’s no secret that ESPN host Stephen A. Smith and NBA star LeBron James don’t get along.

On Monday, Smith defended James after President Donald Trump called James “racist” last week when taking questions from reporters.

This, even for a hot take machine like Smith, was “beyond the pale.”

“It’s embarrassing,” Smith said in a video posted on YouTube. “You’re the commander-in-chief, you’re the president of the United States, and you’re going to come out and you’re going to call this black man, who’s universally recognized one of the greatest athletes who have ever lived, who has been an upstanding citizen, somebody I don’t get along with, and I’m still willing to concede he’s great.”

Smith argued that Trump is resorting to calling James racist simply because James has never supported Trump politically.

James endorsed Hillary Clinton in 2016, Joe Biden in 2020, and Kamala Harris in 2024. 

“The only Democratic candidate LeBron James ever really stood up for was Barack Obama,” Smith said. “Everything since then has basically been anti-Trump over the last three elections.”

Last week, Trump claimed new Philadelphia 76ers superstar might be “a racist” after weighing in on the debate over who is the greatest basketball player of all time.

When Trump responded to the question from Fox News’ Peter Doocy on Friday, the president pointed to his personal relationship and not statistics to settle the debate between James and Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan.

“Well, Michael Jordan’s a guy that’s a friend of mine — play golf with him. He’s a really good guy. And I think LeBron is — maybe he’s a racist. But maybe he doesn’t like Trump, I don’t know. But I only like people that like me. So I would say Michael Jordan all the way,” Trump said.

news.title: GOP Congressman Claims His Opponent Is Under FBI Investigation, But Can’t Prove It
news.text:
WASHINGTON ― Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.) has represented a Democratic-leaning district north of Philadelphia since 2017, repeatedly winning reelection with a combination of a nice guy persona and a bipartisan voting record. 

As he takes on yet another Democratic challenger in the roughest political environment for Republicans in years, Fitzpatrick is heavily pushing a nasty and unproven accusation about his opponent. 

In TV ads, mailers and billboards, Fitzpatrick has said his opponent Bob Harvie, a member of the Bucks County Board of Commissioners, is “under FBI investigation” for corruption. 

There’s not much evidence for the accusation. Harvie did speak to a grand jury in 2022 as part of an investigation into local governments in suburban Philadelphia, though no indictments resulted and the exact targets of the investigation have never been reported. How does Fitzpatrick know the case is still ongoing? 

“I am a former FBI agent, but I know how grand juries work, and I’m well aware of his status in this case,” Fitzpatrick, who worked as a federal prosecutor and FBI agent before running for office in 2017, told HuffPost. “I’m aware of what’s contained in the files that he refuses to release.”

Harvie has furiously denied the accusation and sent a cease-and-desist letter to Fitzpatrick’s campaign, to no avail. 

“He’s desperate to hold on to the seat,” Harvie told HuffPost. “He sees the same polling that I see ― that he’s in trouble, that his party’s in trouble, that Donald Trump is an albatross around the neck of Republicans, and that the policies they put in place are hurting people up and down this county, this district, and that’s why he’s throwing these lies out about me because he doesn’t have anything else to talk about.”

The stakes are high: Fitzpatrick is one of only three Republicans currently representing a district that voted for Kamala Harris in 2024, and Democrats view the seat as an important pickup opportunity in their quest to retake the House this fall. 

Fitzpatrick has broken with his party on all manner of topics, from the war in Iran to gun control to taxes and the social safety net. He voted against final passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill last year, the legislation that slashed food benefits and Medicaid to pay for tax cuts tilted toward the wealthy. But the Fitzpatrick-Harvie showdown so far seems to be mostly about Fitzpatrick’s claim that Harvie is being looked at by the FBI. 

There is no official public information to corroborate or refute the claim that Harvie is under an FBI investigation. The FBI declined to comment.

Harvie has said he testified to the grand jury only as a witness. Fitzpatrick acknowledges Harvie wasn’t the target of the investigation, but insists he’s an investigative subject rather than a mere witness, meaning his conduct is at issue. 

Harvie’s attorney strenuously disagrees: “Harvie is not now and has never been the subject of any criminal investigation,” they wrote in the cease-and-desist letter to Fitzpatrick’s campaign.

“You know what would solve this whole mystery? It’s not a mystery for me, but for you all ― have him release his file,” Fitzpatrick said. He’s also said that if Harvie’s so sure he’s lying, all he has to do is file the lawsuit he’s threatening in his cease-and-desist letter, though the legal process could take weeks, if not months, and not resolve before the election. 

Harvie said there’s no file for him to release, that he doesn’t have any paperwork related to the case. He made some not-so-nice comments of his own about Fitzpatrick.

“He has a $5 million house in California. He’s got a $2 million house in D.C. He’s got another house here in Bucks County that I’m not even sure he lives in,” Harvie said. “He’s obviously now married to a Fox News reporter who’s considerably younger than he is, and so I just think he’s got a lifestyle he likes now, and he’s desperate, you know, and really he’s forgotten about the people of this district.”
